title: Granular control plane rollout automation for private (VPC) upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a robust, repeatable, and safe automation flow for upgrading control plane versions in Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is a Terraform-native interface for operators to declare version intent and rollout policies while an automation controller performs ephemeral canaries, progressive traffic promotion, automated health gating, and safe rollback. This ticket covers module design, orchestration hooks, health probe definitions, and the CI/CD choreography for running a controlled upgrade across customer VPCs without manual per-customer intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module `redwood.private_controlplane_rollout` accepts target_version, canary_group_count, max_parallel_promotions, and health_gate thresholds
Orchestration service can launch ephemeral canary control plane instances (or shadow pods) and route 2-5% of traffic for a configurable canary window
Automated health checks (latency P95, error-rate, kv-cache-hit, model-response-checks) run continuously during the canary window and can block/rollback the promotion
Promotion schedule supports percentage ramping (2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100%) with configurable intervals and automatic gating based on health metrics
Terraform plan/apply is idempotent and writes rollout metadata to the state / rollout registry so upgrades can be audited and resumed
SRE and security review signoff recorded and an automated rollback triggers on predefined SLO regressions or security anomalies
implementation_notes: Terraform: implement a composable module `modules/private/controlplane-rollout` that produces resources: rollout_record (DB entry), canary_instances (in VPC), traffic_policy (edge-proxy config), and health_probe_definition (CloudWatch/Prometheus rules)

Orchestrator: extend existing controlplane operator to support 'ephemeral canary mode' where a small subset of replicas run new version behind a separate service id and share KV caches for realistic traffic priming

Traffic splitting: use VPC edge-proxy (Envoy) weighted routing controlled via config updated by the orchestrator; keep weights stored in Terraform-managed `redwood_rollout` resource so state and auditability align

Health checks: define a standard probe suite: smoke endpoint check, p95 tail latency, 1m error rate, kv-cache warmness (approx TTL hit-rate), and a small deterministic eval set (3 prompts) for regression detection

Gating: implement a 2-tier gate: local (per-customer) health gate and global safety gate. Local gate prevents promotion inside that VPC; global gate halts all ongoing promotions when systemic signals observed
Rollback: orchestrator must support fast rollback command that reverts traffic weights and drains new instances; terraform module exposes an `abort` flag to mark rollout as failed
State & Audit: rollout_record must include start_time, version_from, version_to, step_history, metrics_snapshot and operator (terraform user) so Console can render history
CI: add e2e tests that run on a dedicated private test VPC that simulates tenant traffic patterns; include automated fault injection to verify gating and rollback behavior
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Plan: Operator sets target_version via Terraform and chooses policy: conservative/standard/aggressive
Phase 1 - Canary: Orchestrator provisions ephemeral canary replicas, primes cache, routes 2% traffic for 30m, and runs probe suite every 1m
Phase 2 - Ramp: If canary passes, increment weights to 10% for 1h, then 30% for 2h, with health gates evaluated at each step
Phase 3 - Bulk Promotion: If no regressions, promote remaining capacity in parallel batches limited by max_parallel_promotions configured in module
Phase 4 - Post-Promotion Verification: 24h monitoring window with elevated alerting and automatic snapshot of metrics for audit
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary metrics: p95_latency, p50_latency, request_error_rate, model_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, pod_restart_count
Derived signals: sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_rate (>15% vs baseline), p95 spike >25% absolute, request_error_rate increase >3pp
Alerting: critical PagerDuty trigger for safety-gate breaches, Slack channel automation for rollouts with rollback links
Dashboard: rollout timeline widget, per-VPC comparison, and quick links to the failing probe traces and flamegraphs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Ephemeral canaries might not exercise full production scale -> Mitigation: use synthetic traffic generator that mirrors customer token length distribution and concurrency

Risk: Terraform state drift if orchestrator makes runtime changes -> Mitigation: ensure orchestrator writes a canonical rollout_record and Terraform reads it; avoid direct mutable changes to core resources outside module

Risk: Security exposure while spinning new control plane replicas -> Mitigation: run ephemeral instances in customer's VPC with least-privileged IAM and enforce KMS/HSM policies; security review required
Risk: Slow rollback due to long drain times -> Mitigation: set conservative connection draining and provide rapid kill option for severe regressions
